title: Lost Land (HKAFF)
synopsis:
In a Rohingya refugee camp in Bangladesh, Somira and Shafi share a modest yet happy childhood with their grandfather and grandaunt. One day, carrying their few belongings, the family boards a crowded boat crossing the sea to reunite with their uncle in Malaysia. The siblings cannot understand why strangers treat them like animals, or why the "hometown" the elders speak of feels so far away. Long drawn to the stories of Myanmar and immigrants, Japanese director Akio Fujimoto poignantly captures the cruel realities of the Rohingya people through the innocent eyes of children.

 

Orizzonti Special Jury Prize, Venice International Film Festival

synopsis_lang.zh_hk:
在孟加拉的羅興亞難民營裡，九歲的Somira和四歲的Shafi與兩位老長輩一起生活，小姊弟童年未算無憂卻尚且快樂。一天，他們隨着老人拿起僅餘家當出發，跟身在馬來西亞的叔叔團聚。小姊弟不明白為什麼一家人見面要擠上橫渡安達曼海的船，不明白為什麼陌生大人像動物一樣呼喝拉扯他們，不明白為什麼老人口中的家鄉如此遙遠。與家人一起的地方就是家，但家人又身在何處呢？曾在緬甸生活的日本導演藤元明緒，一直心繫緬甸和移民的故事，也忘不了在當地慘遭剷除的羅興亞族群，透過天真小孩的眼睛展現殘酷現實。

 

威尼斯影展 地平線單元評審團特別獎
